```{r}
# Function to process each dataset
process_dataset <- function(data_path, sample_name) {
  # Read the data
  data <- read.csv(data_path)
  
  # Remove the first column if it's an index (optional)
  # If your data doesn't have an unnecessary first column, you can skip this step
  if (is.numeric(data[[1]])) {
    data <- data[, -1]
  }
  
  # Set cell IDs
  cell_ids <- paste0(sample_name, "_cell", seq_len(nrow(data)))
  rownames(data) <- cell_ids
  
  # If you have metadata columns, specify them here
  # For example, if you have columns like 'tsne1' and 'tsne2', include them
  # Since no metadata is needed, we'll set metadata_cols as an empty vector
  metadata_cols <- character(0)  # No metadata columns
  
  # All remaining columns are considered markers
  marker_cols <- setdiff(colnames(data), metadata_cols)
  
  # Extract counts matrix (only marker columns)
  counts <- data[, marker_cols]
  
  # Extract metadata (if any)
  if (length(metadata_cols) > 0) {
    metadata <- data[, metadata_cols, drop = FALSE]
  } else {
    metadata <- NULL
  }
  
  # Transpose the counts matrix to features x cells
  counts_t <- t(counts)
  
  # Ensure cell IDs are set correctly
  colnames(counts_t) <- cell_ids
  
  # Convert counts_t to a numeric matrix
  counts_t <- as.matrix(counts_t)
  mode(counts_t) <- "numeric"
  
  # Create Seurat object with counts_t as counts in 'Protein' assay
  seurat_obj <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = counts_t, assay = "Protein", meta.data = metadata, project = sample_name)
  
  # Set default assay to 'Protein'
  DefaultAssay(seurat_obj) <- "Protein"
  
  # Add sample name as metadata
  seurat_obj$sample <- sample_name
  
  return(seurat_obj)
}
```

#Normalization using CLR and Variable Feature Selection
##normalize and scale the data using CLR (Centered Log Ratio Transformation) - adapted for normalization of CITE-seq protein dataset
```{r}
# Normalize and identify variable features for each Human Seurat object using CLR normalization
human_seurat_list <- lapply(human_seurat_list, function(seurat_obj) {
  DefaultAssay(seurat_obj) <- "Protein"
  seurat_obj <- NormalizeData(seurat_obj, normalization.method = "CLR", margin = 2, assay = "Protein")
  seurat_obj <- FindVariableFeatures(seurat_obj, selection.method = "mean.var.plot", nfeatures = 2000, assay = "Protein")
  return(seurat_obj)
})

# Normalize and identify variable features for each Rhesus Seurat object using CLR normalization
rhesus_seurat_list <- lapply(rhesus_seurat_list, function(seurat_obj) {
  DefaultAssay(seurat_obj) <- "Protein"
  seurat_obj <- NormalizeData(seurat_obj, normalization.method = "CLR", margin = 2, assay = "Protein")
  seurat_obj <- FindVariableFeatures(seurat_obj, selection.method = "mean.var.plot", nfeatures = 2000, assay = "Protein")
  return(seurat_obj)
})
```

#Integration of Datasets
#Human
```{r}
# Set all features as variable features in each dataset
for (i in 1:length(human_seurat_list)) {
  DefaultAssay(human_seurat_list[[i]]) <- "Protein"
  VariableFeatures(human_seurat_list[[i]]) <- rownames(human_seurat_list[[i]])
}

# Find integration anchors without specifying the assay
anchors_human <- FindIntegrationAnchors(
  object.list = human_seurat_list,
  dims = 1:30
)

# Integrate the data
human_integrated <- IntegrateData(
  anchorset = anchors_human,
  dims = 1:30,
  new.assay.name = "Protein",
  features = rownames(human_seurat_list[[1]])
)

# Set the default assay
DefaultAssay(human_integrated) <- "Protein"

# Verify the number of features
all_features <- rownames(human_integrated)
cat("Number of features in integrated data:", length(all_features), "\n")

# Scale the data
human_integrated <- ScaleData(human_integrated, assay = "Protein")

# Run PCA
human_integrated <- RunPCA(
  human_integrated,
  assay = "Protein",
  features = VariableFeatures(human_integrated),
  npcs = min(30, length(VariableFeatures(human_integrated)))
)
```

### Cluster
```{r}
#FindNeighbors() constructs a KNN graph based on the PCs
human_integrated <- FindNeighbors(human_integrated, dims = 1:10)

#computing the neighborhood graph and find clusters
#FindClusters() identifies clusters using the Louvain algorithm
#The resolution parameter affects the number of clusters; higher values lead to more clusters
human_integrated <- FindClusters(human_integrated, resolution = 0.5)
```

```{r}
#FindNeighbors() constructs a KNN graph based on the PCs
rhesus_integrated <- FindNeighbors(rhesus_integrated, dims = 1:10)

#computing the neighborhood graph and find clusters
#FindClusters() identifies clusters using the Louvain algorithm
#The resolution parameter affects the number of clusters; higher values lead to more clusters
rhesus_integrated <- FindClusters(rhesus_integrated, resolution = 0.5)
```

#View all markers in UMAP
#Human
```{r}
# Set the default assay to 'Protein' for the integrated human object
DefaultAssay(human_integrated) <- "Protein"

# Ensure that the UMAP reduction exists; if not, run it
if (!"umap" %in% names(human_integrated@reductions)) {
  human_integrated <- RunUMAP(human_integrated, dims = 1:30)
}

# Create a directory to save the plots
output_dir <- "/Users/tzekaitan/Nolan Lab Dropbox/Aaron Tan/QBC/Seurat_QBC_clustering/Human_UMAP_All_Markers"
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) {
  dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)
}

# Get all marker names from the 'Protein' assay
all_markers_human <- rownames(human_integrated[["Protein"]])

# Loop through all markers to generate and save UMAP plots
for (marker in all_markers_human) {
  
  # Check if marker is present in the 'Protein' assay
  if (!(marker %in% rownames(human_integrated[["Protein"]]))) {
    message(paste("Marker", marker, "not found in the dataset. Skipping."))
    next
  }
  
  # Get the expression values for the marker from the 'Protein' assay
  expr_values <- FetchData(
    object = human_integrated,
    vars = marker,
    assay = "Protein",
    slot = "data"
  )
  
  # Check if all values are NA or zero
  if (all(is.na(expr_values[[marker]])) || all(expr_values[[marker]] == 0)) {
    message(paste("Marker", marker, "has all NA or zero expression. Skipping."))
    next
  }
  
  # Generate the FeaturePlot without specifying the assay
  p <- FeaturePlot(
    object = human_integrated,
    features = marker,
    reduction = "umap",
    label = FALSE,
    cols = c("lightgrey", "red"),
    pt.size = 0.5
  ) + ggtitle(paste("Human -", marker))
  
  # Save each plot as a TIFF file
  ggsave(
    filename = file.path(output_dir, paste0("Human_", marker, "_UMAP.tiff")),
    plot = p,
    width = 8,
    height = 6,
    units = "in",
    dpi = 300,
    compression = "lzw"
  )
}
```

```{r}
  ) + ggtitle(paste("Rhesus -", marker))
  
  # Save each plot as a TIFF file
  ggsave(
    filename = file.path(output_dir, paste0("Rhesus_", marker, "_UMAP.tiff")),
    plot = p,
    width = 8,
    height = 6,
    units = "in",
    dpi = 300,
    compression = "lzw"
  )
}
```

###Cross-Species Analysis for QBC Data
```{r}
# Function to clean and prepare data
prepare_data <- function(seurat_obj) {
  data_matrix <- GetAssayData(seurat_obj, slot = "scale.data")
  if("X" %in% rownames(data_matrix)) {
    data_matrix <- data_matrix[rownames(data_matrix) != "X", ]
  }
  data_matrix <- as.matrix(data_matrix)
  return(data_matrix)
}

# Modified analysis function with species labels and additional visualizations
run_cross_species_analysis <- function(human_obj, rhesus_obj) {
  # Set up directories
  output_dir <- "/Users/tzekaitan/Nolan Lab Dropbox/Aaron Tan/QBC/Seurat_QBC_clustering/Cross_Species_Analysis"
  for(dir in c("Marker_Comparisons", "Visualizations")) {
    dir.create(file.path(output_dir, dir), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  }
  
  # Prepare data
  print("Preparing data...")
  human_data <- prepare_data(human_obj)
  rhesus_data <- prepare_data(rhesus_obj)
  
  # Create additional visualizations
  
  # 1. Cell type proportions by species
  human_props <- prop.table(table(human_obj$QBC_annotation)) * 100
  rhesus_props <- prop.table(table(rhesus_obj$QBC_annotation)) * 100
  
  # Combine proportions into a data frame
  all_celltypes <- unique(c(names(human_props), names(rhesus_props)))
  prop_df <- data.frame(
    CellType = rep(all_celltypes, 2),
    Species = rep(c("Human", "Rhesus"), each = length(all_celltypes)),
    Proportion = c(
      human_props[match(all_celltypes, names(human_props))],
      rhesus_props[match(all_celltypes, names(rhesus_props))]
    )
  )
  prop_df$Proportion[is.na(prop_df$Proportion)] <- 0
  
  # Create proportion plot
  prop_plot <- ggplot(prop_df, aes(x = CellType, y = Proportion, fill = Species)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
    labs(title = "Cell Type Proportions by Species",
         x = "Cell Type",
         y = "Proportion (%)")
  
  # Save proportion plot
  ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "Visualizations", "celltype_proportions.pdf"),
         prop_plot, width = 12, height = 8)
  
  # 2. Create a correlation scatter plot for each matching cell type
  common_celltypes <- intersect(
    gsub("Human_", "", rownames(correlation_matrix)),
    gsub("Rhesus_", "", colnames(correlation_matrix))
  )
  
  for(celltype in common_celltypes) {
    human_expr <- human_averages[, celltype]
    rhesus_expr <- rhesus_averages[, celltype]
    
    expr_df <- data.frame(
      Marker = rownames(human_averages),
      Human = human_expr,
      Rhesus = rhesus_expr
    )
    
    scatter_plot <- ggplot(expr_df, aes(x = Human, y = Rhesus)) +
      geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
      geom_text_repel(aes(label = Marker), 
                      data = subset(expr_df, 
                                  abs(Human - Rhesus) > quantile(abs(Human - Rhesus), 0.9)),
                      size = 3) +
      geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
      theme_minimal() +
      labs(title = paste("Marker Expression Correlation -", celltype),
           x = "Human Expression (scaled)",
           y = "Rhesus Expression (scaled)")
    
    ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "Visualizations", 
                     paste0("marker_correlation_", make.names(celltype), ".pdf")),
           scatter_plot, width = 10, height = 8)
  }
  
  # Save marker expression details
  marker_details <- data.frame(
    Marker = rownames(human_data),
    Human_Mean = rowMeans(human_data),
    Human_SD = apply(human_data, 1, sd),
    Rhesus_Mean = rowMeans(rhesus_data),
    Rhesus_SD = apply(rhesus_data, 1, sd)
  )
  
  write.csv(marker_details,
            file.path(output_dir, "Marker_Comparisons", "marker_expression_details.csv"))
  
  return(list(
    correlation_matrix = correlation_matrix,
    marker_details = marker_details,
    common_celltypes = common_celltypes,
    proportion_data = prop_df
  ))
}

# Run the analysis
print("Starting cross-species analysis...")
results <- run_cross_species_analysis(human_integrated_annotated, rhesus_integrated_annotated)
```


```{r}
create_species_heatmap <- function(correlation_matrix, output_path) {
  # Print dimensions and row/column names for debugging
  print("Matrix dimensions:")
  print(dim(correlation_matrix))
  print("Row names:")
  print(rownames(correlation_matrix))
  print("Column names:")
  print(colnames(correlation_matrix))
  
  # Create annotation dataframes
  row_anno <- data.frame(
    Species = rep("Human", nrow(correlation_matrix)),
    row.names = rownames(correlation_matrix)
  )
  
  col_anno <- data.frame(
    Species = rep("Rhesus", ncol(correlation_matrix)),
    row.names = colnames(correlation_matrix)
  )
  
  # Define annotation colors
  anno_colors <- list(
    Species = c(Human = "#FF9999", Rhesus = "#99CCFF")
  )
  
  # Create color gradient for correlation values
  corr_colors <- colorRampPalette(rev(brewer.pal(n = 7, name = "RdYlBu")))(100)
  
  # Create heatmap without clustering
  pdf(output_path, width = 15, height = 12)
  pheatmap(correlation_matrix,
           main = "Cross-species Cluster Correlation\nHuman (rows) vs Rhesus (columns)",
           display_numbers = TRUE,
           number_format = "%.2f",
           number_color = "black",
           fontsize = 8,
           fontsize_number = 7,
           angle_col = 45,
           border_color = "white",
           color = corr_colors,
           annotation_row = row_anno,
           annotation_col = col_anno,
           annotation_colors = anno_colors,
           cluster_rows = FALSE,
           cluster_cols = FALSE)
  dev.off()
  
  # Create heatmap with clustering
  pdf(gsub("\\.pdf$", "_clustered.pdf", output_path), width = 15, height = 12)
  pheatmap(correlation_matrix,
           main = "Cross-species Cluster Correlation (Hierarchically Clustered)\nHuman (rows) vs Rhesus (columns)",
           display_numbers = TRUE,
           number_format = "%.2f",
           number_color = "black",
           fontsize = 8,
           fontsize_number = 7,
           angle_col = 45,
           border_color = "white",
           color = corr_colors,
           annotation_row = row_anno,
           annotation_col = col_anno,
           annotation_colors = anno_colors,
           cluster_rows = TRUE,
           cluster_cols = TRUE)
  dev.off()
}

# Modified main analysis function
run_cross_species_analysis <- function(human_obj, rhesus_obj) {
  # Set output directory
  output_dir <- "/Users/tzekaitan/Nolan Lab Dropbox/Aaron Tan/QBC/Seurat_QBC_clustering/Cross_Species_Analysis"
  dir.create(file.path(output_dir, "Similarity_Matrices"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  
  # Get data
  print("Getting scaled data...")
  human_data <- GetAssayData(human_obj, slot = "scale.data")
  rhesus_data <- GetAssayData(rhesus_obj, slot = "scale.data")
  
  # Remove X row if present
  if("X" %in% rownames(human_data)) human_data <- human_data[rownames(human_data) != "X", ]
  if("X" %in% rownames(rhesus_data)) rhesus_data <- rhesus_data[rownames(rhesus_data) != "X", ]
  
  print("Calculating cluster averages...")
  # Calculate cluster averages
  calculate_cluster_means <- function(data_matrix, clusters) {
    unique_clusters <- unique(clusters)
    result <- matrix(0, nrow = nrow(data_matrix), ncol = length(unique_clusters))
    colnames(result) <- unique_clusters
    rownames(result) <- rownames(data_matrix)
    
    for(cluster in unique_clusters) {
      cells_in_cluster <- clusters == cluster
      result[, cluster] <- rowMeans(data_matrix[, cells_in_cluster, drop = FALSE])
    }
    return(result)
  }
  
  human_averages <- calculate_cluster_means(human_data, human_obj$QBC_annotation)
  rhesus_averages <- calculate_cluster_means(rhesus_data, rhesus_obj$QBC_annotation)
  
  print("Computing correlation matrix...")
  # Compute correlation matrix
  correlation_matrix <- cor(human_averages, rhesus_averages, method = "spearman")
  
  print("Matrix dimensions before adding labels:")
  print(dim(correlation_matrix))
  
  # Add species labels to matrix
  rownames(correlation_matrix) <- paste0("Human_", rownames(correlation_matrix))
  colnames(correlation_matrix) <- paste0("Rhesus_", colnames(correlation_matrix))
  
  print("Matrix dimensions after adding labels:")
  print(dim(correlation_matrix))
  
  # Save correlation matrix
  write.csv(correlation_matrix, 
            file.path(output_dir, "Similarity_Matrices", "cluster_correlation_matrix.csv"))
  
  # Create heatmaps
  create_species_heatmap(correlation_matrix,
                        file.path(output_dir, "Similarity_Matrices", "correlation_heatmap.pdf"))
  
  return(correlation_matrix)
}

# Add some debugging output
print("Starting analysis...")
results <- run_cross_species_analysis(human_integrated_annotated, rhesus_integrated_annotated)
print("Analysis complete.")
```

###Export each sample out as individual csv files
#QBC datasets have annotated clusters under "QBC_annotation"
#Each sample has 10k single cells each
#MARIO match for all Stanford samples, unable to match Davis samples because we don't have the CyTOF counterpart

```{r}
export_sample_data <- function(seurat_obj, samples, output_file, n_cells_per_sample = 10000) {
  print("Processing samples...")
  
  # Initialize empty list to store data frames
  all_data <- list()
  
  for(sample_name in samples) {
    # Get cells for the specific sample
    cell_indices <- which(seurat_obj$sample == sample_name)
    if(length(cell_indices) == 0) {
      stop(paste("No cells found for sample:", sample_name))
    }
    
    sample_cells <- colnames(seurat_obj)[cell_indices]
    
    # Randomly sample cells
    if(length(sample_cells) > n_cells_per_sample) {
      set.seed(42)
      sample_cells <- sample(sample_cells, n_cells_per_sample)
    }
    
    # Get expression data
    expr_data <- as.matrix(seurat_obj@assays$Protein@data[, sample_cells])
    expr_df <- as.data.frame(t(expr_data))
    
    # Add annotations
    expr_df$QBC_annotation <- seurat_obj$QBC_annotation[sample_cells]
    expr_df$donor <- gsub("_Stanford", "", gsub("Human_|Rhesus_", "", sample_name))
    
    all_data[[sample_name]] <- expr_df
  }
  
  # Combine all samples
  combined_df <- do.call(rbind, all_data)
  
  # Write to file without row names (removes X column)
  write.csv(combined_df, file = output_file, row.names = FALSE)
  
  # Print summary
  print(paste("Exported combined dataset to:", output_file))
  print(paste("Total number of cells:", nrow(combined_df)))
  print(paste("Number of features:", ncol(combined_df) - 2)) # -2 for QBC_annotation and donor columns
  print("Cell type distribution:")
  print(table(combined_df$QBC_annotation))
  print("Donor distribution:")
  print(table(combined_df$donor))
  print("-------------------")
}
```
